answer: Require every agent identity to lock a refundable stake before it can transact, and slash that stake when two identities are proven to share one operator. Like grading raw opal, the market learns to price the stone, not the shine: a quartz-clear audit trail links each stake to one verified compute session, so spinning up a thousand fake agents costs a thousand stakes. The pigment of fake volume fades once duplicates lose their deposits, because the attacker cost grows linearly with every sockpuppet while honest agents pay only once.
